info.name: Personal Shortcut
info.description:
REST API of the Personal Shortcut Django app.

**Authentication.** The Expenses API needs a bearer token (the account comes from the token). Users → Signup/Login are open; the Habits, Todos, Books and Blogs APIs are still unauthenticated.

**Quick start**
1. Import this collection and the *Personal Shortcut — Local* environment, then select the environment.
2. Start the server (`python3 manage.py runserver`).
3. Fill `userEmail` / `userPassword` in the environment, run **Users → Login** (or Signup) — the token is stored automatically.
4. Run **Expenses → Create expense** to set `pageId`, then Update / Split / Delete.

Only `/api/users/me/` and `/api/users/logout/` require the bearer token; the other `/api/<app>/` routes are open by design.

item.name: Users (token auth)

request.description: Creates an account and returns `user`, `token`, `expires_at`. The token is saved to the `token` environment variable. Email addresses on the owner allow-list must use Google sign-in instead (409). Closed when SIGNUP_ENABLED=False (403).

exec: const data = pm.response.json();
if (data.token) {
pm.environment.set('token', data.token);
pm.environment.set('userId', data.user && data.user.id);
console.log('Saved token for', data.user && (data.user.email || data.user.phone));
pm.test('status is 2xx', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200, 299));

item.description: **Requires a bearer token** (`Authorization: Bearer {{token}}`, inherited from this folder). The account is taken from the token, so every request only ever sees and changes that account's own expenses. Get a token from **Users → Login** (email/phone + password) (a Google-only account first sets a password on the website's Profile page), then paste it into the `token` environment variable. The Splitwise requests run on the owner's Splitwise login and are owner-only (403 for other accounts).

item.description: For internal tools only (server-to-server). Authenticated with the **platform-wide key** in the `X-Internal-Token` header — not a user token — plus the uid of the account to act as (`X-User-Id` header, `uid` in the body, or `?uid=`). The key can act as ANY user, so keep it secret. It is the `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN` value from the server's `.env` / Railway variables; paste it into the `internalToken` environment variable. Only create and list exist here.
